Alright, I've just finished the code edits: the viewmodel anchoring in hud.js, the synthwave music generator in audio.js, added a music volume setting in settings.js, and patched main.js to start the music and to unlock the pointer when the buy menu opens. All those changes were applied successfully, but I haven't actually verified that they work in the running game yet. The user asked for the gun to be positioned correctly (which is handled by the viewmodel fix) and for free background music (handled by the synthwave loop), plus they want the pointer not to lock behind the shop popup. I need to confirm all three aspects in a real playtest.

The best way to do that is to spin up the server, launch the game in a headless Chrome instance via Puppeteer, and take screenshots at both an ultrawide resolution (to see the viewmodel scaling and placement) and a standard 16:9 resolution (to ensure nothing broke there). I also want to query the game's audio system to verify that the music is indeed playing and that the new music volume setting is respected.

Looking at the repository, there’s a test directory that already contains some tooling for automated tests, but I don’t see a script that captures screenshots with custom viewports. I’ll create a temporary script in test called dbg-uw.mjs that does exactly what I need. The script will:

1. Spawn the server (`node server/index.js`) from the app directory, forcing it onto a known port (3974) so I can reliably connect to it.
2. Wait a short period (≈900 ms) for the server to start listening.
3. Launch Chrome via Puppeteer with the required flags (`--no-sandbox`, `--use-gl=angle`, etc.) and set the viewport to an ultrawide size (1998 × 769) which matches the user’s ultrawide monitor.
4. Navigate to the game’s root URL and wait for the `window.GAME` object to be ready.
5. Use the built‑in test API (`GAME.test`) to set graphics to the “balanced” preset (so visual quality is consistent), start a game on the “canopy” map, skip the buy menu (so we can get straight into gameplay), and pose the player at a known orientation (`pose(0, 0, 18, 0, -0.02)`) that will display the gun in view.
6. After a brief pause (≈1200 ms) to let the frame render, take a screenshot (`dbg-uw.png`) of the ultrawide view.
7. Then switch the viewport to a standard 1280 × 720 size, wait a bit, and capture another screenshot (`dbg-169.png`) for comparison.
8. Finally, evaluate `GAME.test.sfxReport().music` to fetch the current music state and log it, confirming that our synthwave loop is active.
9. Clean up by closing the browser and killing the server process.

I’ll embed this whole script as a heredoc into a Bash command that writes the file and then runs it with Node. The command needs a generous timeout (240 seconds) because launching Chrome and rendering can be a bit slow, especially on CI runners. This approach gives me concrete visual evidence (the two screenshots) and a programmatic check (the music report) that all three user requests are satisfied.

Now I’ll issue the Bash tool call to create and execute this script.
